notes: Use a Navigo Easy with a t+ carnet on the metro; take RER C to Versailles and RER B to CDG (11 EUR). The city is walkable: don't take the metro for 20-minute distances.
Timed online tickets are essential for the Louvre, Orsay and Sainte-Chapelle. The Louvre is closed on Tuesdays and Orsay on Mondays. The Paris Museum Pass is available for 2 to 6 days.
Summer brings 25-30°C and daylight until 22:00. Head to the Seine banks (Paris Plages), picnics and terraces. Some bistros close for holiday in August.
A bistro set lunch (formule) costs 18-25 EUR, about half the price of dinner. Tap water (carafe d'eau) is free; for a tip, just round up the bill.
Bouillons (Chartier, Racine) are cheap and classic; go for falafel in the Marais and croissants at Pain Pain or Du Pain et des Idées.
Watch out for pickpockets on metro line 1 and in Montmartre; wear your backpack on your front.

transit.name: Navigo Easy / t+ carnet
transit.why_chosen: Covers metro, RER and buses; a carnet of 10 is the most practical option, with an extra ticket needed for RER C to Versailles.
transit.coverage: Paris metro, otobüs, tramvay, RER zone 1
transit.where_to_buy: Metro istasyonları biletmatik; Navigo Easy kartı 2 EUR

stops.name: Louvre Müzesi
stops.tips: Head straight for the Mona Lisa, then the Denon wing. Book a timed ticket online (32 EUR for non-EU visitors); the Carrousel entrance has no queue.

stops.name: Jardin des Tuileries
stops.tips: Stroll through the gardens from the Louvre to Concorde; look for the green chairs.

stops.name: Café Kitsuné Palais Royal
stops.tips: Coffee and a sandwich in the Palais Royal garden, in a colonnaded courtyard.

stops.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
stops.tips: Monet's Water Lilies in oval rooms; right next to the Louvre and quiet.

stops.name: Eiffel Tower
stops.tips: Take the stairs to the 2nd floor, then the lift to the summit (combined ticket ~29 EUR). Book online and go at sunset; take photos from Trocadéro.

backups.name: Le Petit Cler
backups.tips: A bistro on Rue Cler, close to the Eiffel Tower.

backups.name: Champ de Mars
backups.tips: Lawns beneath the tower; picnic here and watch the light show (every hour on the hour).

days.theme: Île de la Cité, Latin Quarter and Saint-Germain

stops.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
stops.tips: The restored cathedral is free; reserve a time slot online. Mornings are quiet.

stops.name: Sainte-Chapelle
stops.tips: 1,113 stained-glass panels, at their best on a sunny morning. Book online.

stops.name: Shakespeare and Company
stops.tips: The legendary English-language bookshop on the banks of the Seine.

stops.name: Le Comptoir du Panthéon
stops.tips: A bistro opposite the Panthéon, with steak-frites and a terrace.

stops.name: Panthéon
stops.tips: The tombs of Voltaire, Hugo and Curie; Foucault's pendulum.

backups.name: Bouillon Racine
backups.tips: An Art Nouveau bouillon with an inexpensive classic French menu.

backups.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
backups.tips: The Senate gardens, with a pond and chairs; go here instead of the Panthéon.

stops.name: Sacré-Cœur
stops.tips: The basilica is free; the dome costs 8 EUR. The steps are empty in the morning, with views over Paris.

stops.name: Place du Tertre
stops.tips: The painters' square; portraits cost 40-60 EUR, and you can haggle.

stops.name: Montmartre Vineyard and Lapin Agile
stops.tips: Paris's last vineyard and a cabaret, on Rue des Saules.

stops.name: Chantoiseau Montmartre
stops.tips: A neo-bistro 7 minutes from Place du Tertre, with a set lunch menu.

stops.name: Musée de Montmartre
stops.tips: Renoir's studio and gardens, with views over the vineyard.

backups.name: Boulangerie Pain Pain
backups.tips: Award-winning baguettes and pastries; a quick lunch.

backups.name: Moulin Rouge
backups.tips: See it from outside in Pigalle; the evening show is extra (~120 EUR).

stops.name: Place des Vosges
stops.tips: The oldest square in Paris, with arcades and Victor Hugo's house (free).

stops.name: Musée Picasso Paris
stops.tips: The Picasso collection in the Hôtel Salé. Book online.

stops.name: L'As du Fallafel
stops.tips: The falafel place on Rue des Rosiers with a queue out front; eat standing up.

stops.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
stops.tips: The oldest market in Paris, with Moroccan, Japanese and Lebanese stalls.

stops.name: Centre Pompidou
stops.tips: Inside-out architecture, modern art and views of Paris from the terrace. It is under renovation in 2025-30; if it is closed, go to the Bourse de Commerce.

backups.name: Bourse de Commerce Pinault Collection
backups.tips: Tadao Ando's concrete cylinder and contemporary art; the alternative if the Pompidou is closed.

backups.name: Au Petit Versailles du Marais
backups.tips: Award-winning croissants and quiche; an alternative to the falafel.

stops.name: Musée d'Orsay
stops.tips: Impressionists in a former railway station. Van Gogh is on the 5th floor; photograph the clock face. Book online.

stops.name: Rue du Bac & Le Bon Marché
stops.tips: The Grande Épicerie food hall; good for souvenirs.

stops.name: Café de Flore
stops.tips: Saint-Germain's literary café; try the croque monsieur and hot chocolate.

stops.name: Pont des Arts and the Seine Embankment
stops.tips: See the Île de la Cité from the bridge, then walk along the riverside path.

stops.name: Bateaux Parisiens Seine Cruise
stops.tips: A 1-hour river cruise; Notre-Dame and the Eiffel Tower in sunset light. Board at the Eiffel Tower pier.

backups.name: Bateaux Mouches
backups.tips: The other cruise company, boarding at Pont de l'Alma.

backups.name: La Grande Épicerie de Paris
backups.tips: The food hall at Le Bon Marché; have lunch at the counters instead of Café de Flore.

stops.name: Palace of Versailles
stops.tips: 45 minutes by RER C. Get the palace, gardens and Trianon passport (~32 EUR); the Hall of Mirrors is empty when it opens at 09:00.

stops.name: Gardens of Versailles
stops.tips: Le Nôtre's gardens; in summer, the musical fountain days (extra ticket).

stops.name: La Flottille Versailles
stops.tips: A restaurant beside the Grand Canal, with rowing boats for hire next door.

stops.name: Petit Trianon and Hameau de la Reine
stops.tips: Marie Antoinette's hamlet and the queen's farm; included with the passport.

stops.name: Marché Notre-Dame Versailles
stops.tips: A food market in town; pick up cheese on your way back.

backups.name: Angelina Versailles
backups.tips: Hot chocolate and Mont-Blanc inside the palace.

backups.name: Grand Trianon
backups.tips: A pink marble pavilion; go here instead of the Petit Trianon.

days.theme: Canal Saint-Martin and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Canal Saint-Martin
stops.tips: Iron footbridges and canal locks; have a morning coffee and spot the Amélie film locations.

stops.name: Du Pain et des Idées
stops.tips: One of the best bakeries in Paris; try the chocolate-pistachio escargot.

stops.name: Marché d'Aligre
stops.tips: A daily market at Bastille, good for cheese and food souvenirs.

stops.name: Le Baron Rouge
stops.tips: A wine bar next to the Aligre market; oysters and wine from the barrel for a farewell.

stops.name: Gare du Nord / RER B
stops.tips: RER B to CDG takes 35 minutes. Goodbye, Paris.

backups.name: Coulée Verte René-Dumont
backups.tips: A green walkway on a former railway line; go here instead of Aligre.
